vedic_reference.note: The name Athmika is derived from the Sanskrit word आत्मा (Atma) which means self, soul, or principle. It is derived from the root आधार (Adhara) which means base or foundation.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Athmika" has its roots deeply embedded in Hindu culture, reflecting the significance of the self or soul in Hindu philosophy. It emphasizes the importance of self-awareness and introspection, which are essential aspects of many Hindu spiritual practices. Further, the name signifies a transcendental connection to one's inner self and the divine existence, reflecting the soul's eternal nature.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Athmika" carries a profound spiritual significance. In Hinduism, the soul, often represented by the Atman, is believed to be eternal, unchanging, and divine. By embracing the name "Athmika," one affirms their connection to their soul and embarks on a spiritual journey towards self-realization and union with the divine. The name serves as a constant reminder of the soul's divine nature and the ultimate quest for self-discovery and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Athmika was a queen of the Satavahana dynasty, ruling between 110 AD and 130 AD. The name Athmika carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Satavahana dynasty was an important political power in ancient India during the period of the Indian subcontinent known as the Satavahana period, which lasted from 230 BC to 220 AD.

historical_references.reference: Athmika is also believed to be the wife of Ashoka the Great's grandson, Emperor Dasaratha, and is mentioned in the Ashokan inscriptions as a patron of the Buddhist faith.
historical_references.context: Ashoka the Great was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty, who ruled from 268 BC to 232 BC. His grandson, Dasaratha, ruled in the 2nd century BC and was a great patron of Buddhism.
